title: Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: A strong business can still be a broken chart.
epigraph.author: Market maxim

book_paragraphs: Between the 12 November 2026 baseline dossier and the 25 November 2026 live snapshot, TD Power Systems' technical structure deteriorated from a contested pullback into a confirmed Stage 4 breakdown. On the 2026-11-23 NSE market-facts ledger cutoff, the stock closed at ₹605.30—clinging just above its 200-day simple moving average of ₹599.03 while market_facts classified the trend as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback). Two sessions later, on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, the stock fell another 3.02% to ₹587.05, decisively slicing below both its 200-day SMA (₹601.31) and its TradingView daily S1 pivot (₹599.53). It has also dropped off TheWrap Stage 2 leaderboard (`in_thewrap_stage2: false`), ending its prior 82-week Stage 2 run.

The moving-average stack now confirms unambiguous Stage 4 supply dominance. At the 2026-11-25 live close of ₹587.05, TDPS trades 5.49% below its 10-day SMA (₹621.12), 9.32% below its 20-day SMA (₹647.39), and 17.39% below a falling 50-day SMA (₹710.59). On the weekly chart—the primary Weinstein timeframe—price sits 11.12% below its 10-week EMA (₹660.51), 11.84% below its 30-week SMA (₹665.91), and 3.49% below its 40-week EMA (₹608.25). Every short-, medium-, and long-term trend filter now sits overhead as potential resistance. Consequently, the technical timing engine locks the stock at STAGE_4, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, and CAP_REJECTED.

Relative strength and institutional distribution tell the same story. Against a Nifty 50 benchmark that remains in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) regime—with 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks above their 50-day SMA, 48.2% above their 200-day SMA, 7 of 11 sectors above key averages, and only 3 distribution days in the last 25 sessions—TDPS has severely underperformed. On the 2026-11-23 market-facts ledger, TDPS logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions, a 63-day relative strength of -24.31%, and a 28-day relative strength of -40.04% versus the Nifty 50. That divergence proves the sell-off is not merely a broad market sneeze; institutional capital is actively rotating out of the stock.

Public ownership filings corroborate the tape's distribution footprint. Through 13 November 2026, Oxbow Capital Management reduced its institutional holding from 3.08% to 1.42% via open-market sales, offloading 1.66% of the company right around the Q2 FY2027 earnings release [45]. Trading volume on the 2026-11-25 drop to ₹587.05 was 4.93 million shares—0.74x the 30-day average of 6.67 million shares, though the 10-day average volume jumped to 11.03 million shares during the post-earnings liquidation wave. Heavy turnover on declining prices followed by weak, lower-volume drift below the 200-day SMA is classic institutional supply absorption without aggressive dip-buying.

The multi-timeframe momentum read shows oversold tension without any confirmed turn. On the 2026-11-25 live snapshot, daily RSI(14) fell to 37.03, weekly RSI(14) slipped to 44.35, and 4-hour RSI(14) sits at 37.86. Price at ₹587.05 remains well below the 4-hour EMA20 (₹620.33) and 4-hour SMA50 (₹655.70), so the intraday engine flags `intraday_4h_turn: false`. Meanwhile, the 14-day Average True Range (ATR) is elevated at ₹38.53 (roughly 6.6% of live price), and Bollinger Band width has expanded to 34.83%. Buying into high volatility without a confirmed higher low on the 4-hour and daily charts is catching a falling knife.

Yet the oversold extension (-17.39% below the 50-day SMA, daily RSI 37.03) creates a crucial tactical distinction between new capital and existing holdings. For new capital, the rule is absolute: STAGE_4 and CAP_REJECTED prohibit any purchase. No entry zone is active; the ₹550–₹575 band referenced in the execution table is strictly a historical 20-day swing-low reference shelf (around the ₹557.05 swing low), not a buy order. New capital cannot reconsider TDPS until it stops making lower lows, carves out a multi-week Stage 1 base, reclaims its 200-day and 50-day averages on expanding volume, and clears a fresh valuation check.

For the existing 470-share Zerodha position (average cost ₹636.52, portfolio weight 6.67% on the 2026-11-23 ledger), selling blindly at ₹587.05 into an oversold air pocket is equally undisciplined. Notice the exact map of nearby levels. Directly below ₹587.05 lies the 20-day swing low at ₹557.05. Just beneath that shelf sits our ratcheted hard-stop invalidation at ₹545.00—raised upward by +₹25.00 (+4.8%) from the prior dossier's ₹520.00 structural stop to respect the upward-only stop-loss ratchet while staying safely below live CMP and normal 1-ATR noise. Below ₹545.00, the next major technical air pocket runs all the way down to the TradingView daily S2 pivot at ₹485.17.

Above ₹587.05, the broken 200-day SMA (₹601.31) and broken 40-week EMA (₹608.25) form immediate overhead resistance well below the 4-hour EMA20 (₹620.33) and daily 20-day SMA (₹647.39). Holding all 470 shares for a ₹620.00 bounce against a ₹545.00 stop yields only +₹32.95 upside versus -₹42.05 downside—an unfavorable 0.78:1 bounce-versus-stop ratio in an unhedged Stage 4 stock with a 6.56% daily ATR (₹38.53). We therefore tighten our exit into two strict tranches: sell 235 shares (50%) immediately at market (~₹587.05) to halve Stage 4 weight from 6.67% to ~3.3%, and exit the remaining 235 shares into broken 200D/40W resistance (₹601–₹615, alert ₹605.00) or below the ₹545.00 hard stop.

Let's check the exact wallet math on this tightened two-tranche exit. Selling 235 shares immediately at ~₹587.05 realizes ~₹11,625 of loss (vs ₹636.52 avg cost) and immediately cuts unhedged stop-gap dollar exposure in half. On the remaining 235 shares, exiting into ₹605.00–₹615.00 recovers +₹17.95 to +₹27.95 per share (+₹4,218 to +₹6,568), while the ratcheted ₹545.00 hard stop caps residual incremental downside at -₹42.05 per share (-7.16%, or -₹9,882). Even an unhedged 1-ATR overnight gap (-₹38.53, or -6.56%) now costs roughly -₹9,055 rather than -₹18,109, protecting the portfolio ahead of the ₹485 S2 pivot.

The options overlay remains straightforward and unchanged. According to the 2026-11-25 options snapshot (`options_IN_batch2.json`), TDPOWERSYS is not included in the NSE F&O segment and has no liquid listed options chain. Its options status is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID. Investors cannot buy protective puts to hedge the 470-share holding, nor can they express a defined-risk rebound thesis through call spreads or LEAPS. Every rupee of exposure is pure cash equity with linear downside, which makes strict adherence to the ₹545.00 hard stop non-negotiable.

Finally, remember what a stop-loss alert can and cannot do in a mid-cap industrial stock with a ₹38.53 daily ATR. A ₹545.00 hard stop is a confirmed daily/weekly closing invalidation rule, not a guarantee against overnight gap-down risk if negative tariff or earnings headlines hit outside NSE trading hours. Because TDPS is a 6.67% tactical momentum position in a confirmed Stage 4 markdown, the burden of proof has shifted completely onto the bulls. Until the stock reclaims ₹660+ (above its 10-week EMA and 30-week SMA) with rising relative strength and institutional accumulation, every rally into broken 200D/40W resistance (₹601–₹615) is an exit opportunity, not a reason to add.

To monitor whether a genuine Stage 1 base eventually forms months from now, track four objective tape signals in sequence. First, price must hold above ₹545.00–₹557.05 on a multi-week basis while daily ATR contracts below ₹25. Second, 25-day distribution days must fall from 7 back to 3 or fewer as volume dries up on red sessions. Third, price must reclaim the 200-day SMA (₹601.31) and 50-day SMA (₹710.59) on above-average volume (>1.5x 30-day average). Fourth, 63-day relative strength versus the Nifty 50 must turn positive. None of those four conditions exists today, which is why the technical verdict is unequivocally REJECTED for new capital and EXIT_ON_BOUNCE for held shares.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a former leader loses its 200-day average and drops off the Stage 2 list while the broad market stays in an uptrend, stop arguing with the tape. Protect capital first: use oversold bounces to exit into overhead supply, and never lower a structural stop.
